paper_metadata.title: Effect of normalizing temperature on the strengthening mechanisms of the advanced Re-containing 10 %Cr steel with low N and high B contents

evidence.quote: Effect of different normalizing temperature ranging from 1050 to 1200 ◦C on the structure and tensile properties of the Re-containing 10 %Cr steel was investigated.
The heat treatment consisted of normalizing at 1050 ◦C, 1100 ◦C, 1150 ◦C and 1200 ◦C for 1 h with following tempering at 770 ◦C for 3 h, air cooling.

EBSD demonstrated the increase in the fraction of low-angle boundaries (LABs) from 2 to 5◦ corresponding to misorientation of martensitic laths by 16% and the distance between HABs by 33%, as NT increased from 1050 ◦C to 1200 ◦C
The engineering stress-elongation curves ( Fig. 3 a,b) represented + 10% increases in both yield strength (YS) and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) at 20 ◦C, as NT increased to 1100 ◦C.
High volume fraction of nano-scaled M23C6 provided the high contribution of particle strengthening of 143 and 181 MPa after NT at 1050 ◦C and 1100 ◦C, respectively.
